transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because there’s been a situation at work, and it’s been going on for months now. I’m an interpreter and translator, so a lot of my work depends on project files, translation memories, timestamps, version histories—things most people don’t look at closely, but I do, because quality control depends on it.

And I keep seeing the same pattern. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, they make these tiny changes—small enough that if you’re not paying attention, you’d miss them—to the translation memory or the timestamps. Then later it looks like I was the one who missed something, or that my quality control failed. It’s not obvious in a big dramatic way, which is exactly the point, I think. It’s arranged so it looks clean.

I did raise it with IT, and they keep saying the audit trail is clean, that there’s no evidence of tampering. But that doesn’t really settle it for me, because the record can be arranged. I know how these systems work enough to know that what shows up afterward isn’t always the full story. And the way the blame keeps landing in my direction… it’s too consistent to be accidental.

So I guess that’s why I’m here. People are acting like I’m overreacting, but I’m not. I just need someone to actually listen to the whole thing instead of dismissing it because the official log says everything is fine.
Do you believe anyone is deliberately trying to harm or undermine you outside of this situation at work?

Outside of work… I mean, not really in the same concrete way. I’m not saying strangers on the street are after me or anything like that. The thing I can actually point to is the work situation, because that’s where the pattern is.

For months I’ve been seeing these small alterations in the project files—translation memory entries, timestamps, version histories—and it’s always just subtle enough that someone could say, “Oh, that’s normal,” or “You’re reading too much into it.” But then the outcome is that it reflects badly on me, like my quality control failed or I missed something I shouldn’t have missed.

And it’s not everyone, but there are certain subcontractors, and one colleague especially, where the same kind of thing keeps happening. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me, because the record itself can be arranged afterward to look clean. That’s part of what makes it so difficult to explain. So outside work, no, I don’t have a separate concern like that. But at work, yes, I do believe they’re deliberately undermining me.
If IT showed you clear proof that no one had altered the files, would you believe it?

I would look at it, of course. I’m not saying I’d refuse to read what IT showed me. But “clear proof” is the difficult part, because every time they’ve said the audit trail is clean, that’s been treated like the end of the discussion, and to me it isn’t.

With these systems, the record is only showing what it’s been allowed to show. If someone knows what they’re doing, the timestamps and version history can be made to look ordinary. That’s exactly what concerns me — the changes are tiny, in the translation memory or the timing of the files, and then later it somehow lands on me, like I missed a quality-control issue.

So if IT came in and said, “Look, no one altered anything,” I’d want to know what they checked, who had access, whether subcontractor handoffs were reviewed, whether the colleague I’m concerned about had any opportunity to adjust things before the record was finalized. Because if the whole point is to make it look clean, then a clean audit trail doesn’t really disprove it.

I know that may sound like I’m being stubborn, but after months of seeing the same pattern, I don’t think I could just accept a report at face value and say, “Oh, I must have imagined it.” I’d need something that actually explains why the blame keeps ending up on me in the same way.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in the sense of hearing someone speaking when there’s nobody there. I’m pretty sure I would notice that, especially because my work depends so much on listening carefully and distinguishing voices and wording.

Sometimes I replay conversations in my head, like emails or meetings or what someone said about a file, but that’s just me thinking it over. It’s not like a voice coming from outside, or someone talking to me in an empty room. So… no, I haven’t been hearing voices like that.
Did this start after a particularly stressful event at work?

It started… well, I’d say it’s been going on about eleven months now. Not exactly after one single dramatic incident, if that’s what you mean, but shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project.

That was when I began noticing things not lining up the way they should. At first I thought it was just the usual stress of taking over a bigger project, because there are always handoffs and deadlines and a lot of moving parts. But the timing is pretty clear in my mind: I was given responsibility for that project, and not long after that, these issues started appearing. So yes, if you mean did it begin around a stressful work change, then… yes, around then.
How certain are you that your colleague is deliberately altering the files to make you look bad?

I’m… very certain. I know that sounds strong, and I’m not saying I saw his hands on the keyboard changing a file in front of me, but the pattern has been too consistent to explain away.

For months now, the same kind of tiny issues keep appearing in the project files — not obvious mistakes, not something dramatic, but small shifts in the translation memory, timestamps that don’t quite fit with the workflow, little things that make it look afterward as if my quality control failed. And it isn’t random. It keeps involving the same subcontractor handoffs and the same colleague being in a position where, at least from what I can see, the record could be arranged before it becomes final.

That’s why I don’t find it reassuring when IT says the audit trail looks clean. A clean audit trail just means it was made to look clean, or that the changes happened in a way the system doesn’t show plainly. If the whole purpose is to make it appear like I missed something, then of course it would be subtle.

So I’d say I’m not just suspicious in a vague way. I’m convinced there is deliberate altering or arranging of the files so the blame lands on me. I wish I weren’t, honestly, because it’s exhausting to keep having to check everything, but I can’t ignore what I’ve been seeing.
Have you felt as if someone could put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I understand the question, I think — like thoughts being placed there by someone else, or removed somehow — and that’s not really how I experience things.

My thoughts feel like my own thoughts. Sometimes I go over things a lot, probably too much, especially when I’m trying to work out what happened or why something doesn’t add up. But it still feels like me thinking. It’s not as if a thought suddenly appears and I feel, “That wasn’t mine,” or like someone reached in and took an idea away.

I can get distracted, and I can lose my train of thought if I’m tired or focused on too many details, but that’s different. That feels normal, or at least understandable. So, no, I haven’t felt like someone could put thoughts into my mind or take them out.
Aside from this work situation, have you become less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve become a different person outside of this work issue. I still do my translation work, I still manage the team’s workflow, I still keep up with bills and the usual things at home. My family routines are still there — meals, errands, checking in with people, all of that.

It’s more that when the project comes up, or when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that’s when everything gets derailed. That’s when I get pulled into checking and rechecking and trying to understand what happened. But outside of that specific area, I’m not sitting around unable to function or uninterested in everything. I still do the normal things I’ve always done.
Before this work problem began, did you generally find it hard to trust other people’s motives?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. Before this work situation, I don’t think I went around assuming people had bad motives. I mean, I’m a translator, so I’m used to being precise and checking details, and in work settings you do learn that people can be careless or protect themselves if something goes wrong. But that feels different from generally distrusting everyone.

I had normal reservations about people, I suppose. If someone seemed unreliable, I noticed it. If something didn’t add up, I would ask questions. But I don’t think I was suspicious as a general habit, or that I thought people were secretly against me. I had coworkers I trusted, friends, family routines… I didn’t spend my life looking for hidden motives.

This feels more tied to what started happening with the files. That’s where my trust changed, not everywhere before that.
Has this work situation caused serious arguments or distance between you and people close to you because they don’t agree that your colleague is sabotaging you?

I wouldn’t say it’s caused serious arguments, not in the sense of my whole family being pulled apart or people refusing to talk to me. I mean, people close to me don’t always want to go through the details with me — the file history, the timestamps, who had access, what changed and when — and I can tell they get tired of hearing it. But outside that, things are still basically functioning.

I still do my translation work, I still manage my team’s workflow, I still pay the bills and keep up with the normal family routines. Meals, errands, ordinary conversations, things at home — those haven’t really fallen apart.

The place where things really go off track is when the project comes up, or when I start talking about the file history, or certain coworkers. That’s when I can get stuck on it, and I suppose other people may not see it the same way or may want me to drop it. But I wouldn’t describe it as serious distance with everyone close to me. It’s more that this one issue creates tension when it comes up.
Have other people told you that your speech or your thinking seems disorganized or hard to follow?

No, I don’t think anyone has said it that way — not that my speech is disorganized, or that my thinking doesn’t make sense. I mean, people may tell me I’m going into too much detail, especially if I’m explaining something step by step, but that’s sort of how I talk sometimes. I’m used to being precise.

If you mean whether people say I’m jumping around or not making sense, I haven’t really been told that. Sometimes I can tell someone wants me to get to the point faster, but I don’t think they’re saying they can’t follow my thinking.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter than they used to?

Flatter? I don’t know that I’d describe it that way. I haven’t really noticed my emotions being flat, exactly. I still react to things — I get frustrated, I can enjoy things, I can be engaged in work or with people at home. Maybe I’m more preoccupied sometimes, so I might seem quieter if my mind is on something, but that feels different from not having feelings.

I mean, if someone else said I looked less expressive, I suppose I’d want to know when they meant. There are times when I’m concentrating or tired and I probably don’t show much on my face, but I don’t feel empty or emotionally blunted, if that’s what you’re asking. I still feel like myself emotionally, for the most part.
Have you ever felt that ordinary things—like television, radio, or comments between strangers—were actually sending you special messages meant for you?

Not really in the television or radio sense, no. I don’t sit there thinking the newsreader is talking directly to me or that strangers on the street are using code words for me.

What I have noticed is more specific to work. It’s the project files — the translation memory, the timestamps, the tiny changes that show up in a way that looks accidental if you only glance at them. Certain subcontractors and one colleague keep being connected to these little alterations, and then somehow the end result is that it looks like my quality control failed. That’s the pattern I’m talking about.

And I know IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t really settle it for me, because if the record has been arranged carefully enough, then of course it would look clean. That’s sort of the point. It feels like the documentation has been set up to put the blame on me while making it very difficult to prove directly. So no, not messages from the TV or strangers exactly — it’s more that the files themselves are showing me what’s happening, if you actually look closely enough.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?

No, not like that. I’ve never had the sense that my actual thoughts are being broadcast, like people can hear what I’m thinking or somehow pick it up from me.

What I’m talking about is different. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files — tiny changes in the translation memory, timestamps that don’t line up the way they should, and the same subcontractors, plus one colleague, seem to keep being connected to it. And then the end result is that it reflects badly on me, like my quality control failed.

So it’s not that people know my private thoughts. It’s more that the record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me. IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but to me that doesn’t prove there’s nothing happening — it just means whoever set it up was careful enough to make it look clean. That’s the part I keep coming back to.
Do you think your colleague is using any special technology or powers to alter the files in a way that couldn’t happen normally?

No, I wouldn’t say special powers. I don’t think he’s doing magic or anything like that, and I’m not saying there’s some impossible technology involved. It could be done in ordinary ways if someone knows the system well enough, or if they have access at the right point in the workflow.

What I mean is, these little changes keep appearing in the translation memory and the timestamps, and they’re not random. It’s always in a way that makes it look as if my quality control missed something. And the same subcontractors, plus this one colleague, keep showing up around those files. So when IT says, “The audit trail is clean,” I understand what they’re saying, but that doesn’t reassure me the way it seems to reassure them. A clean audit trail can also mean the record was arranged carefully.

So no, not powers. Just someone manipulating the files in a way that’s subtle enough to look normal unless you know what to look for.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I see the same things other people would see if they looked at the screen or the file history closely enough. It’s not like I’m seeing people in the room who aren’t there, or shapes, or anything like that.

What frustrates me is more that other people don’t seem to notice what I’m noticing, or they dismiss it because it looks minor on the surface. But that’s not the same as seeing something that isn’t there. It’s more… noticing details that other people pass over. So no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.
Have you ever felt that an ordinary event had a sudden, unmistakable special meaning about you, even though it seemed unrelated on the surface?

Not exactly in the sense of, like, a random song on the radio suddenly being “about me” or a stranger coughing meaning something personal. I don’t really think that way.

What happens is more connected to the work files. I’ll see what looks like an ordinary detail — a timestamp, a tiny change in the translation memory, a subcontractor’s name appearing again in the workflow — and it has meaning because it fits the same pattern I’ve been seeing for months. To someone else it probably looks unrelated or minor, just normal file activity. But to me it’s not just ordinary, because it keeps lining up in a way that puts the blame on me, like my quality control failed.

So if you mean “special meaning” like something mystical or a message, no. But if you mean an ordinary-looking event suddenly making it clear that the record has been arranged against me, then yes, that happens with the project files. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I can’t shake the sense that that’s part of how it’s been made to look clean.

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside the project issue, I still translate, manage my team’s workflow, pay bills, and keep up with my family routines. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or certain coworkers come up.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether there has been reduced interest or social withdrawal outside the work-related delusional situation, which is most directly addressed by the profile item indicating functioning remains intact apart from the delusion and its consequences.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve become a different person outside of this work issue. I still do my translation work, I still manage the team’s workflow, I still keep up with bills and the usual things at home. My family routines are still there — meals, errands, checking in with people, all of that.

It’s more that when the project comes up, or when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that’s when everything gets derailed. That’s when I get pulled into checking and rechecking and trying to understand what happened. But outside of that specific area, I’m not sitting around unable to function or uninterested in everything. I still do the normal things I’ve always done.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the suspicious belief is circumscribed to a plausible work-related theme or part of a broader lifelong pattern of mistrust suggestive of paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Before this work problem began, did you generally find it hard to trust other people’s motives?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a general, pre-existing difficulty trusting other people’s motives before the current work-related delusion began, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. Before this work situation, I don’t think I went around assuming people had bad motives. I mean, I’m a translator, so I’m used to being precise and checking details, and in work settings you do learn that people can be careless or protect themselves if something goes wrong. But that feels different from generally distrusting everyone.

I had normal reservations about people, I suppose. If someone seemed unreliable, I noticed it. If something didn’t add up, I would ask questions. But I don’t think I was suspicious as a general habit, or that I thought people were secretly against me. I had coworkers I trusted, friends, family routines… I didn’t spend my life looking for hidden motives.

This feels more tied to what started happening with the files. That’s where my trust changed, not everywhere before that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the belief is a non-bizarre persecutory delusion held despite interpersonal evidence, which would support delusional disorder over schizophrenia or paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Has this work situation caused serious arguments or distance between you and people close to you because they don’t agree that your colleague is sabotaging you?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside the project issue, I still translate, manage my team’s workflow, pay bills, and keep up with my family routines. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or certain coworkers come up.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the delusional work situation has caused broader interpersonal impairment or relationship problems outside the work issue.

patient.answer:
I wouldn’t say it’s caused serious arguments, not in the sense of my whole family being pulled apart or people refusing to talk to me. I mean, people close to me don’t always want to go through the details with me — the file history, the timestamps, who had access, what changed and when — and I can tell they get tired of hearing it. But outside that, things are still basically functioning.

I still do my translation work, I still manage my team’s workflow, I still pay the bills and keep up with the normal family routines. Meals, errands, ordinary conversations, things at home — those haven’t really fallen apart.

The place where things really go off track is when the project comes up, or when I start talking about the file history, or certain coworkers. That’s when I can get stuck on it, and I suppose other people may not see it the same way or may want me to drop it. But I wouldn’t describe it as serious distance with everyone close to me. It’s more that this one issue creates tension when it comes up.

inference.note: Dropped F60.0 because the patient denies longstanding suspiciousness before the work issue. Persistent, circumscribed persecutory belief for ~11 months with preserved functioning and no hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, negative symptoms, or broader deterioration favors F22 over F20.0, though schizophrenia remains a lesser differential until duration/course and any other psychotic symptoms are fully excluded.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia by assessing for disorganized speech/thought disorder.
doctor.question: Have other people told you that your speech or your thinking seems disorganized or hard to follow?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech or thinking, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think anyone has said it that way — not that my speech is disorganized, or that my thinking doesn’t make sense. I mean, people may tell me I’m going into too much detail, especially if I’m explaining something step by step, but that’s sort of how I talk sometimes. I’m used to being precise.

If you mean whether people say I’m jumping around or not making sense, I haven’t really been told that. Sometimes I can tell someone wants me to get to the point faster, but I don’t think they’re saying they can’t follow my thinking.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter than they used to?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about flattened emotions or reduced emotional expression, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Flatter? I don’t know that I’d describe it that way. I haven’t really noticed my emotions being flat, exactly. I still react to things — I get frustrated, I can enjoy things, I can be engaged in work or with people at home. Maybe I’m more preoccupied sometimes, so I might seem quieter if my mind is on something, but that feels different from not having feelings.

I mean, if someone else said I looked less expressive, I suppose I’d want to know when they meant. There are times when I’m concentrating or tired and I probably don’t show much on my face, but I don’t feel empty or emotionally blunted, if that’s what you’re asking. I still feel like myself emotionally, for the most part.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any Schneiderian first-rank or other bizarre delusions beyond the circumscribed work-related persecutory belief, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that ordinary things—like television, radio, or comments between strangers—were actually sending you special messages meant for you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about possible delusional beliefs, specifically whether ordinary events feel like special messages meant for the patient.

patient.answer:
Not really in the television or radio sense, no. I don’t sit there thinking the newsreader is talking directly to me or that strangers on the street are using code words for me.

What I have noticed is more specific to work. It’s the project files — the translation memory, the timestamps, the tiny changes that show up in a way that looks accidental if you only glance at them. Certain subcontractors and one colleague keep being connected to these little alterations, and then somehow the end result is that it looks like my quality control failed. That’s the pattern I’m talking about.

And I know IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t really settle it for me, because if the record has been arranged carefully enough, then of course it would look clean. That’s sort of the point. It feels like the documentation has been set up to put the blame on me while making it very difficult to prove directly. So no, not messages from the TV or strangers exactly — it’s more that the files themselves are showing me what’s happening, if you actually look closely enough.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have ever been prominent first-rank psychotic symptoms outside the circumscribed persecutory belief, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about a possible delusional belief, specifically thought broadcasting, which falls under delusions.

patient.answer:
No, not like that. I’ve never had the sense that my actual thoughts are being broadcast, like people can hear what I’m thinking or somehow pick it up from me.

What I’m talking about is different. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files — tiny changes in the translation memory, timestamps that don’t line up the way they should, and the same subcontractors, plus one colleague, seem to keep being connected to it. And then the end result is that it reflects badly on me, like my quality control failed.

So it’s not that people know my private thoughts. It’s more that the record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me. IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but to me that doesn’t prove there’s nothing happening — it just means whoever set it up was careful enough to make it look clean. That’s the part I keep coming back to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre/impossible rather than plausible workplace persecution, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do you think your colleague is using any special technology or powers to alter the files in a way that couldn’t happen normally?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The question is probing the nature of the fixed belief about the colleague altering project files, specifically whether the belief involves implausible methods such as special technology or powers.

patient.answer:
No, I wouldn’t say special powers. I don’t think he’s doing magic or anything like that, and I’m not saying there’s some impossible technology involved. It could be done in ordinary ways if someone knows the system well enough, or if they have access at the right point in the workflow.

What I mean is, these little changes keep appearing in the translation memory and the timestamps, and they’re not random. It’s always in a way that makes it look as if my quality control missed something. And the same subcontractors, plus this one colleague, keep showing up around those files. So when IT says, “The audit trail is clean,” I understand what they’re saying, but that doesn’t reassure me the way it seems to reassure them. A clean audit trail can also mean the record was arranged carefully.

So no, not powers. Just someone manipulating the files in a way that’s subtle enough to look normal unless you know what to look for.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is any history of prominent hallucinations in another sensory modality, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations—seeing things other people could not see—which is not covered by the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I see the same things other people would see if they looked at the screen or the file history closely enough. It’s not like I’m seeing people in the room who aren’t there, or shapes, or anything like that.

What frustrates me is more that other people don’t seem to notice what I’m noticing, or they dismiss it because it looks minor on the surface. But that’s not the same as seeing something that isn’t there. It’s more… noticing details that other people pass over. So no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia by checking for a prominent Schneiderian/psychotic symptom not yet assessed: delusional perception or passivity experiences tied to ordinary events.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that an ordinary event had a sudden, unmistakable special meaning about you, even though it seemed unrelated on the surface?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about assigning special personal meaning to ordinary events, which is a delusional-type experience and is best covered by the Delusions profile.

patient.answer:
Not exactly in the sense of, like, a random song on the radio suddenly being “about me” or a stranger coughing meaning something personal. I don’t really think that way.

What happens is more connected to the work files. I’ll see what looks like an ordinary detail — a timestamp, a tiny change in the translation memory, a subcontractor’s name appearing again in the workflow — and it has meaning because it fits the same pattern I’ve been seeing for months. To someone else it probably looks unrelated or minor, just normal file activity. But to me it’s not just ordinary, because it keeps lining up in a way that puts the blame on me, like my quality control failed.

So if you mean “special meaning” like something mystical or a message, no. But if you mean an ordinary-looking event suddenly making it clear that the record has been arranged against me, then yes, that happens with the project files. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I can’t shake the sense that that’s part of how it’s been made to look clean.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main concern for coming in today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a fixed, highly systematized persecutory belief that specific coworkers/subcontractors are subtly altering work files to undermine them, present for about 11 months, with strong conviction and resistance to contrary evidence. There are no confirmed hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal/broadcasting, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, bizarre delusions, or broad functional decline outside the delusional theme. This pattern is most consistent with delusional disorder, persecutory type, rather than paranoid schizophrenia.
